title: Announcing Perspec 1.0
excerpt: Perspec is a desktop app for correcting the perspective of images. After 9 years of development, version 1.0 is finally here.
content_html:
2026-07-29 — 3020 Words — 16 min

I'm very excited to announce the 1.0 release of Perspec!

Perspec is a desktop app for correcting the perspective of images. This is primarily useful for photos of documents and receipts, but it can be used for any kind of image.

This has finally become the app I envisioned when I started working on the project 9 years ago. I didn't think it would take me this long to get here, but I'm very happy with the result and I hope you'll like it too!

Initial Motivation

You're probably familiar with the scanner apps available for mobile phones, like Adobe Scan, vFlat, SwiftScan, … and numerous others. Scanning functionality is also integrated into Dropbox, and these days even natively into iOS itself.

However, I don't like working on my phone and I'd rather just take photos of the documents and receipts and deal with cleaning them up and organizing them on my computer another day. There, I have a big screen, a keyboard, and a precise mouse, which makes editing faster and more accurate.

Also, the mobile apps make some annoying technical decisions in the name of giving users something they're familiar with.

For example: If you store a document as a grayscale PNG, you can get small file sizes without introducing any compression artifacts. However, all the popular apps will give you a grayscale JPEG image with a much bigger file size and worse image quality, just because JPEG is what people are familiar with.

Or maybe I'm giving them too much credit and they actually don't know that PNGs can be smaller than JPEGs if the image contains large areas of uniform color, whereas for normal photos, JPEGs are smaller than PNGs. And no, converting it to PNG afterwards is not an option, as by then the image already contains all the JPEG compression artifacts.

For example, let's compare the results of scanning the following document:

The other apps produce bigger files, and you can clearly see the compression artifacts that degrade the result.

Another thing that annoys me more than it should is the ridiculous detection previews that seemingly every app includes these days:

While you're taking a photo, the app shows you a live overlay of where it detects the document. This, however, doesn't help you at all. Just because it can detect the document correctly in the preview video feed doesn't mean it will detect it correctly in the final photo. Due to the higher resolution, different lighting (exposure times, flash, …), and different contrast, the detection will often be quite different in the final photo.

So all the preview is telling you is that there is indeed a document in front of your camera, which you already know since you placed it there. 🤦‍♂️

Lastly, and most importantly, I knew I could build a better document detection algorithm for the kind of photos I was taking. The detection in existing apps would often be slightly off, even if you had a good picture with good contrast between the document and the background.

Most apps use some kind of edge detection step in their pipeline, as Dropbox explains here. But I knew that documents and receipts often don't have straight edges but rather wrinkled or curved ones. When you try to match even just a slight curve with a straight line, the endpoints will be quite far off. So instead, the app should try to detect the corners and build up the document from there. There is a detailed explanation of the computer vision techniques later in the post.

The Long Road to 1.0

I was still a student when I started working on Perspec and had to scan a lot of stuff for my studies, so I had plenty of motivation to build something like this.

Sure, you could also fix the perspective with Photoshop, Affinity Photo, or GIMP. But the overhead is substantial: Open each photo, find the perspective tool, drag the corners, pick the right export settings, repeat for the next photo, and so on. These tools are built to do everything with any image and not to churn through 50 receipts as quickly as possible. I wanted an app that's focused on this one task, with a workflow that's as streamlined as possible.

My first iteration was a fully automatic CLI app called Perspectra, implemented with Python and scikit-image. You'd pass your image and it would try to detect and extract the document for you. Simple as that.

Although I actually liked scikit-image — feature-rich, yet more straightforward than OpenCV — I quickly realized that I absolutely do not like Python. But more importantly, I realized that I also needed a GUI to fix incorrectly detected document boundaries, as the fully automatic CV pipeline would never get all documents 100% right.

And how do you build a desktop app with a GUI? Obviously with Haskell. 😝 Joking aside, I had recently started learning Haskell and was absolutely in love with it. So naturally, I wanted to see if it could be used for building the desktop app.

As I didn't want to use Python any longer, my next instinct was to use ImageMagick for the computer vision and image manipulation tasks, as I had some experience with its features and capabilities. The existing Haskell bindings were rather lacking, so I opted to simply call magick as an external process. While this mostly worked, it was always a pain to get it installed and linked correctly across platforms, and the performance was surprisingly bad for larger images.

Another obvious choice would have been OpenCV, but I had some bad memories of using it at university (maybe it was just the C++ context …), and the Haskell bindings looked rather painful.

So, my next experiment was using the native Haskell image processing library Hip. With the help of its author @lehins himself and @HanStolpo, we were able to make it work at ZuriHac! (Thanks again!)

However, it was still missing some features that I wanted, like binarization with Otsu's Method. While it was certainly possible to implement this in Hip, I (for once) felt that Haskell's abstractions didn't really help with the task at hand and only complicated things unnecessarily. A for loop in C, by comparison, is conceptually very simple and just as fast as the Haskell code. Luckily, C is a first-class citizen in Haskell and it's very easy to bundle some C code and call it via Haskell's FFI.

Unfortunately, there didn't seem to be a straightforward C library that I could hook up to Perspec without too many FFI headaches, and so I started working on FlatCV — a pure C library for computer vision and image manipulation.

I might have overdone it with the yak shaving here, but since the whole project is a labor of love anyway, why not go all the way? 😅

I'm quite happy with the experience of using C for the image manipulation algorithms, and I was able to quickly build a fully functioning version with the necessary Haskell bindings. Just recently, I released version 0.3.0, and by now it has most of the basic operations you would expect from an image manipulation library. I also ported some of the higher-level CV operations, like adaptive binarization and corner detection, that I first implemented in Perspectra.

There are still plenty of opportunities to improve the performance of FlatCV: SIMD, GPU usage, streamed processing, etc. However, as FlatCV isn't used in a real-time context (i.e., 60 fps), the performance is already more than sufficient.

With FlatCV in place, I could finally implement the last missing piece for 1.0: Automatic corner detection directly in Perspec.

Edge Detection vs. Corner Detection

Most scanner apps detect documents with a pipeline along the lines of the one described by Dropbox:

  1. Downscale the image
  2. Run an edge detection algorithm (e.g. Canny)
  3. Find the most prominent straight lines with a Hough transform
  4. Build quadrilaterals from the intersections of those lines and score them to pick the best one

This works great for a perfectly flat sheet of paper on a high-contrast background. But real documents are rarely perfectly flat: Receipts are wrinkled, book pages are curved, and paper that has been folded never lies completely flat either. When you fit a straight line to a curved edge, the intersections of the lines (i.e. the reconstructed corners) can be quite off, even if the edge detection itself was perfect.

Perspec therefore approaches it from the other side: Instead of looking for straight edges, it segments the photo into document and background and then derives the corners from the document's outline. This is FlatCV's corner detection pipeline in detail:

  1. Convert the image to grayscale and downscale it to 256×256 px. (The detection doesn't need the full resolution, and this makes it fast.)
  2. Blur the image to get rid of noise and paper texture.
  3. Create an elevation map with a Sobel filter. (Strong edges become mountain ridges.)
  4. Flood the elevation map with watershed segmentation: The center of the image seeds the document basin and the image border seeds the background basin. The result is a binary mask of the document.
  5. Smooth the mask with a binary closing.
  6. Run a Förstner corner detector on the mask. (Unlike the more popular Harris detector, whose corners are shifted inwards, the Förstner detector yields sub-pixel-accurate corner positions.)
  7. Sort the corner candidates and keep the 4 corners with the largest angles.
  8. Scale the corner coordinates back up to the original resolution.
Input Detected Corners

The nice thing about this approach is that it never assumes straight edges. The watershed happily follows a wrinkled document boundary, and even on a crumpled receipt the corners are still locally well defined.

And if the detection does get it wrong, you can simply drag the selection polygon into the right size and position. The best of both worlds: automatic detection and manual correction.

Binarization Algorithms

Correcting the perspective is only half the story. For documents and receipts, the other half is converting the photo into a clean black & white image. This is what the Save BW and Save BW Smooth buttons in Perspec do.

The task sounds trivial: Every pixel darker than some threshold becomes black and every other pixel becomes white. The tricky part is picking the threshold.

The classic solution is Otsu's Method: It builds a histogram of all gray values in the image and then picks the threshold that best separates the dark pixels (the text) from the bright pixels (the paper). This works well … for evenly lit images.

Unfortunately, photos are seldom evenly lit. There is often a brightness gradient or a shadow cast by the person that's holding the camera or the camera itself.

The document scanning literature is full of locally adaptive algorithms (e.g. Niblack and Sauvola) that compute an individual threshold for every pixel based on its neighborhood.

FlatCV's smart black & white conversion, however, uses a simpler trick to get away with a single global threshold: It removes the shadows before thresholding.

  1. Convert the image to grayscale.
  2. Create a heavily blurred copy of it (with a blur radius of roughly 10% of the image size). All the text and details get averaged away and what remains is basically just the illumination: brightness gradients and soft shadows.
  3. Subtract the blurred copy from the grayscale image. This keeps the high frequencies (the text) and removes the low frequencies (the shadows). The result is an evenly lit image.
  4. Apply a global threshold calculated with Otsu's Method.

For photos of printed documents, I've found this to work just as well as — or even better than — the more complicated locally adaptive algorithms, while being faster and simpler to implement.

The Save BW button applies exactly this pipeline and stores the result as a true 1-bit black & white image, where every pixel is either fully black or fully white.

The new Save BW Smooth button goes one step further and uses two thresholds (the Otsu threshold ± a small offset): Pixels below the lower threshold become black, pixels above the upper threshold become white, and pixels in between keep a scaled gray value. This yields anti-aliased edges, so the text doesn't look jagged, while the file size stays almost as small. That's why it's the recommended option for documents, receipts, and whiteboards.

Input
Save BW
Save BW Smooth

What Else Is New in 1.0

The automatic corner detection is the headline feature, but quite a few other things landed in the 1.0 release:

  • Support for Windows. With macOS and Linux already covered, Perspec now runs on all 3 major desktop operating systems.
  • The edges of the selection polygon can now be dragged as well (previously only the corners), and grid lines make it easier to align the selection.
  • A new "Select Files" view with a button and drag-and-drop support for selecting images.
  • The new Save BW Smooth export option that converts the image to anti-aliased black & white. This is now the recommended option for documents, receipts, and whiteboards.
  • EXIF rotation data is now also handled for PNGs.
  • An upgrade to the latest version of Brillo, which brings an improved app design, button hover effects, and per-OS default fonts.

Check out the changelog for the full list of changes.

Installation

Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Windows, and Linux are also available on the releases page, and on macOS you can install it via my Homebrew tap:

brew install --cask ad-si/tap/perspec

However, you'll still need to buy a license to get rid of the upgrade banner in those versions.

You can purchase a license for Perspec on either itch.io or Gumroad. This gets you a license key, which removes the annoying "please buy a license" messages in the app.

And even if you don't need the software yourself, please consider buying it as a way to support the development of Haskell desktop applications and computer vision software.

Once installed, you can either drop images onto the app window or batch process them via the CLI:

perspec fix photos/*.jpeg

Next Steps

While the 1.0 release is a big milestone, there are still some features that I would like to add. Here is what I have planned for the upcoming releases:

  • Fixed output sizes: Force the output to standardized dimensions like A4 or US Letter, so a scanned document ends up with the correct proportions and size.
  • QR code detection: Marcel Robitaille wrote a great post about automating receipt ingestion where a QR code next to the document is used to attach metadata. I'd love to support such workflows out of the box.

If this sounds useful to you, give Perspec a try! And if you run into any issues or have ideas for improvements, please open an issue — I'd love to hear your feedback!

If you have any comments, thoughts, or other feedback feel free to write me @AdrianSieber. Thanks for your help! 😊

blocks.html_en: Another thing that annoys me more than it should is the ridiculous detection previews that seemingly every app includes these days:

sentences.en: Another thing that annoys me more than it should is the ridiculous detection previews that seemingly every app includes these days:

blocks.html_en: While you're taking a photo, the app shows you a live overlay of where it detects the document. This, however, doesn't help you at all. Just because it can detect the document correctly in the preview video feed doesn't mean it will detect it correctly in the final photo. Due to the higher resolution, different lighting (exposure times, flash, …), and different contrast, the detection will often be quite different in the final photo.

sentences.en: While you're taking a photo, the app shows you a live overlay of where it detects the document.
sentences.zh: 当您拍照时，该应用程序会向您显示检测到文档的实时叠加图。

sentences.en: This, however, doesn't help you at all.
sentences.zh: 然而，这对你根本没有帮助。

sentences.en: Just because it can detect the document correctly in the preview video feed doesn't mean it will detect it correctly in the final photo.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为它可以在预览视频源中正确检测到文档并不意味着它会在最终照片中正确检测到它。

sentences.en: Due to the higher resolution, different lighting (exposure times, flash, …), and different contrast, the detection will often be quite different in the final photo.

blocks.html_en: So all the preview is telling you is that there is indeed a document in front of your camera, which you already know since you placed it there. 🤦‍♂️

sentences.en: So all the preview is telling you is that there is indeed a document in front of your camera, which you already know since you placed it there. 🤦‍♂️

blocks.html_en: Lastly, and most importantly, I knew I could build a better document detection algorithm for the kind of photos I was taking. The detection in existing apps would often be slightly off, even if you had a good picture with good contrast between the document and the background.

sentences.en: Lastly, and most importantly, I knew I could build a better document detection algorithm for the kind of photos I was taking.
sentences.zh: 最后，也是最重要的，我知道我可以为我拍摄的照片类型构建更好的文档检测算法。

sentences.en: The detection in existing apps would often be slightly off, even if you had a good picture with good contrast between the document and the background.
sentences.zh: 即使您有一张文档与背景之间对比度良好的好图片，现有应用程序中的检测通常也会略有偏差。

blocks.html_en: Most apps use some kind of edge detection step in their pipeline, as Dropbox explains here. But I knew that documents and receipts often don't have straight edges but rather wrinkled or curved ones. When you try to match even just a slight curve with a straight line, the endpoints will be quite far off. So instead, the app should try to detect the corners and build up the document from there. There is a detailed explanation of the computer vision techniques later in the post.

sentences.en: Most apps use some kind of edge detection step in their pipeline, as Dropbox explains here.
sentences.zh: 大多数应用程序在其管道中使用某种边缘检测步骤，正如 Dropbox 所解释的那样。

sentences.en: But I knew that documents and receipts often don't have straight edges but rather wrinkled or curved ones.

sentences.en: When you try to match even just a slight curve with a straight line, the endpoints will be quite far off.
sentences.zh: 当您尝试将一条轻微的曲线与直线匹配时，端点将相距甚远。

sentences.en: So instead, the app should try to detect the corners and build up the document from there.
sentences.zh: 因此，应用程序应该尝试检测角点并从那里构建文档。

sentences.en: There is a detailed explanation of the computer vision techniques later in the post.
sentences.zh: 文章后面有对计算机视觉技术的详细解释。

blocks.html_en: Sure, you could also fix the perspective with Photoshop, Affinity Photo, or GIMP. But the overhead is substantial: Open each photo, find the perspective tool, drag the corners, pick the right export settings, repeat for the next photo, and so on. These tools are built to do everything with any image and not to churn through 50 receipts as quickly as possible. I wanted an app that's focused on this one task, with a workflow that's as streamlined as possible.

sentences.en: Sure, you could also fix the perspective with Photoshop, Affinity Photo, or GIMP.
sentences.zh: 当然，您也可以使用 Photoshop、Affinity Photo 或 GIMP 修复透视。

sentences.en: But the overhead is substantial: Open each photo, find the perspective tool, drag the corners, pick the right export settings, repeat for the next photo, and so on.

sentences.en: These tools are built to do everything with any image and not to churn through 50 receipts as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 这些工具旨在对任何图像执行所有操作，而不是尽快翻阅 50 张收据。

sentences.en: I wanted an app that's focused on this one task, with a workflow that's as streamlined as possible.
sentences.zh: 我想要一款专注于这一任务的应用程序，并具有尽可能简化的工作流程。

blocks.html_en: My first iteration was a fully automatic CLI app called Perspectra, implemented with Python and scikit-image. You'd pass your image and it would try to detect and extract the document for you. Simple as that.

sentences.en: My first iteration was a fully automatic CLI app called Perspectra, implemented with Python and scikit-image.
sentences.zh: 我的第一次迭代是一个名为 Perspectra 的全自动 CLI 应用程序，使用 Python 和 scikit-image 实现。

sentences.en: You'd pass your image and it would try to detect and extract the document for you.
sentences.zh: 您将传递您的图像，它会尝试为您检测并提取文档。

sentences.en: Simple as that.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: Although I actually liked scikit-image — feature-rich, yet more straightforward than OpenCV — I quickly realized that I absolutely do not like Python.

sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，我意识到我还需要一个 GUI 来修复错误检测到的文档边界，因为全自动 CV 管道永远无法让所有文档 100% 正确。

blocks.html_en: And how do you build a desktop app with a GUI? Obviously with Haskell. 😝 Joking aside, I had recently started learning Haskell and was absolutely in love with it. So naturally, I wanted to see if it could be used for building the desktop app.

While this mostly worked, it was always a pain to get it installed and linked correctly across platforms, and the performance was surprisingly bad for larger images.

sentences.en: However, it was still missing some features that I wanted, like binarization with Otsu's Method.

sentences.en: Just recently, I released version 0.3.0, and by now it has most of the basic operations you would expect from an image manipulation library.

blocks.html_en: Edge Detection vs. Corner Detection

sentences.en: Edge Detection vs. Corner Detection
sentences.zh: 边缘检测与角点检测

blocks.html_en: Most scanner apps detect documents with a pipeline along the lines of the one described by Dropbox:

sentences.en: Most scanner apps detect documents with a pipeline along the lines of the one described by Dropbox:
sentences.zh: 大多数扫描仪应用程序都会使用 Dropbox 描述的管道来检测文档：

blocks.html_en: • Downscale the image

sentences.en: Downscale the image
sentences.zh: 缩小图像

blocks.html_en: • Run an edge detection algorithm (e.g. Canny)

sentences.en: Run an edge detection algorithm (e.g. Canny)
sentences.zh: 运行边缘检测算法（例如 Canny）

blocks.html_en: • Find the most prominent straight lines with a Hough transform

sentences.en: Find the most prominent straight lines with a Hough transform
sentences.zh: 使用霍夫变换找到最突出的直线

blocks.html_en: • Build quadrilaterals from the intersections of those lines and score them to pick the best one

sentences.en: Build quadrilaterals from the intersections of those lines and score them to pick the best one
sentences.zh: 从这些线的交点构建四边形并对它们进行评分以选择最佳的四边形

blocks.html_en: This works great for a perfectly flat sheet of paper on a high-contrast background. But real documents are rarely perfectly flat: Receipts are wrinkled, book pages are curved, and paper that has been folded never lies completely flat either. When you fit a straight line to a curved edge, the intersections of the lines (i.e. the reconstructed corners) can be quite off, even if the edge detection itself was perfect.

sentences.en: This works great for a perfectly flat sheet of paper on a high-contrast background.
sentences.zh: 这对于高对比度背景上完美平坦的纸张非常有效。

sentences.en: But real documents are rarely perfectly flat: Receipts are wrinkled, book pages are curved, and paper that has been folded never lies completely flat either.
sentences.zh: 但真正的文件很少是完全平坦的：收据是皱巴巴的，书页是弯曲的，折叠后的纸张也永远不会完全平坦。

sentences.en: When you fit a straight line to a curved edge, the intersections of the lines (i.e. the reconstructed corners) can be quite off, even if the edge detection itself was perfect.
sentences.zh: 当您将直线拟合到弯曲边缘时，即使边缘检测本身是完美的，线的交点（即重建的角）也可能会非常偏离。

blocks.html_en: Perspec therefore approaches it from the other side: Instead of looking for straight edges, it segments the photo into document and background and then derives the corners from the document's outline. This is FlatCV's corner detection pipeline in detail:

sentences.en: Perspec therefore approaches it from the other side: Instead of looking for straight edges, it segments the photo into document and background and then derives the corners from the document's outline.
sentences.zh: 因此，Perspec 从另一面着手：它不是寻找直边，而是将照片分割为文档和背景，然后从文档的轮廓中导出角点。

sentences.en: This is FlatCV's corner detection pipeline in detail:
sentences.zh: 这是 FlatCV 角点检测流程的详细信息：

blocks.html_en: • Convert the image to grayscale and downscale it to 256×256 px. (The detection doesn't need the full resolution, and this makes it fast.)

sentences.en: Convert the image to grayscale and downscale it to 256×256 px.
sentences.zh: 将图像转换为灰度并将其缩小为 256×256 像素。

sentences.en: (The detection doesn't need the full resolution, and this makes it fast.)
sentences.zh: （检测不需要全分辨率，这使得检测速度更快。）

blocks.html_en: • Blur the image to get rid of noise and paper texture.

sentences.en: Blur the image to get rid of noise and paper texture.
sentences.zh: 模糊图像以消除噪音和纸张纹理。

blocks.html_en: • Create an elevation map with a Sobel filter. (Strong edges become mountain ridges.)

sentences.en: Create an elevation map with a Sobel filter.
sentences.zh: 使用 Sobel 过滤器创建高程图。

sentences.en: (Strong edges become mountain ridges.)
sentences.zh: （坚固的边缘成为山脊。）

blocks.html_en: • Flood the elevation map with watershed segmentation: The center of the image seeds the document basin and the image border seeds the background basin. The result is a binary mask of the document.

sentences.en: Flood the elevation map with watershed segmentation: The center of the image seeds the document basin and the image border seeds the background basin.
sentences.zh: 使用分水岭分割淹没高程图：图像中心为文档盆地播种，图像边界为背景盆地播种。

sentences.en: The result is a binary mask of the document.
sentences.zh: 结果是文档的二进制掩码。

blocks.html_en: • Smooth the mask with a binary closing.

sentences.en: Smooth the mask with a binary closing.
sentences.zh: 使用二元闭合平滑蒙版。

blocks.html_en: • Run a Förstner corner detector on the mask. (Unlike the more popular Harris detector, whose corners are shifted inwards, the Förstner detector yields sub-pixel-accurate corner positions.)

sentences.en: Run a Förstner corner detector on the mask.

2026-07-29 — 3020 字 — 16 分钟

我非常高兴地宣布 Perspec 1.0 版本发布！

Perspec 是一款用于校正图像透视的桌面应用程序。 这主要用于文档和收据的照片，但它可以用于任何类型的图像。

这终于成为我 9 年前开始做这个项目时所设想的应用程序。 我没想到我会花这么长时间才到达这里，但我对结果非常满意，我希望你也会喜欢它！

最初的动机

您可能熟悉适用于手机的扫描仪应用程序，例如 Adob​​e Scan、vFlat、SwiftScan…… 以及许多其他人。 扫描功能也集成到 Dropbox 中，如今甚至原生集成到 iOS 本身中。

然而，我不喜欢在手机上工作，我宁愿只拍摄文件和收据的照片，并在另一天清理它们并在计算机上整理它们。 在那里，我有一个大屏幕、一个键盘和一个精确的鼠标，这使得编辑更快、更准确。

此外，移动应用程序以向用户提供他们熟悉的东西的名义做出了一些烦人的技术决策。

例如：如果将文档存储为灰度 PNG，则可以获得较小的文件大小，而不会引入任何压缩伪影。 然而，所有流行的应用程序都会给你一个灰度JPEG图像，文件大小更大，图像质量更差，只是因为JPEG是人们所熟悉的。

或者也许我给了他们太多的信任，他们实际上不知道如果图像包含大面积的统一颜色，PNG 可以比 JPEG 小，而对于普通照片，JPEG 比 PNG 小。 不，之后将其转换为 PNG 不是一个选择，因为到那时图像已经包含所有 JPEG 压缩伪影。

例如，我们来比较一下扫描以下文档的结果：

其他应用程序会生成更大的文件，您可以清楚地看到降低结果质量的压缩伪影。

App 结果 预览 Notes
佩斯佩克 ~110 kB，PNG 查看结果
扫描仪专业版 ~190 kB，JPEG 查看结果 从导出的 PDF 中提取 JPEG
iOS ~300 kB，JPEG 查看结果 从导出的 PDF 中提取 JPEG

另一件让我更烦恼的事情是现在似乎每个应用程序都包含可笑的检测预览：

当您拍照时，该应用程序会向您显示检测到文档的实时叠加图。 然而，这对你根本没有帮助。 仅仅因为它可以在预览视频源中正确检测到文档并不意味着它会在最终照片中正确检测到它。 由于分辨率较高、光照不同（曝光时间、闪光灯等）以及对比度不同，最终照片中的检测结果通常会有很大不同。

因此，所有预览都在告诉您，相机前面确实有一个文档，自从您将其放置在那里以来，您就已经知道了该文档。 🤦‍♂️

最后，也是最重要的，我知道我可以为我拍摄的照片类型构建更好的文档检测算法。 即使您有一张文档与背景之间对比度良好的好图片，现有应用程序中的检测通常也会略有偏差。

大多数应用程序在其管道中使用某种边缘检测步骤，正如 Dropbox 所解释的那样。 但我知道文件和收据通常没有直边，而是有皱纹或弯曲的边缘。 当您尝试将一条轻微的曲线与直线匹配时，端点将相距甚远。 因此，应用程序应该尝试检测角点并从那里构建文档。 文章后面有对计算机视觉技术的详细解释。

通往 1.0 的漫长道路

当我开始研究 Perspec 时，我还是一名学生，为了学习不得不扫描很多东西，所以我有足够的动力去构建这样的东西。

当然，您也可以使用 Photoshop、Affinity Photo 或 GIMP 修复透视。 但开销是巨大的：打开每张照片，找到透视工具，拖动角，选择正确的导出设置，重复下一张照片，等等。 这些工具旨在对任何图像执行所有操作，而不是尽快翻阅 50 张收据。 我想要一款专注于这一任务的应用程序，并具有尽可能简化的工作流程。

我的第一次迭代是一个名为 Perspectra 的全自动 CLI 应用程序，使用 Python 和 scikit-image 实现。 您将传递您的图像，它会尝试为您检测并提取文档。 就这么简单。

虽然我实际上很喜欢 scikit-image——功能丰富，但比 OpenCV 更简单——但我很快意识到我绝对不喜欢 Python。 但更重要的是，我意识到我还需要一个 GUI 来修复错误检测到的文档边界，因为全自动 CV 管道永远无法让所有文档 100% 正确。

如何构建带有 GUI 的桌面应用程序？ 显然是用哈斯克尔。 😝 开玩笑吧，我最近开始学习 Haskell 并且非常喜欢它。 很自然地，我想看看它是否可以用于构建桌面应用程序。

由于我不想再使用 Python，我的下一个本能是使用 ImageMagick 来执行计算机视觉和图像处理任务，因为我对其特性和功能有一些经验。 现有的 Haskell 绑定相当缺乏，所以我选择简单地调用 magick 作为外部进程。 虽然这大部分有效，但跨平台正确安装和链接它总是很痛苦，而且对于较大的图像来说，性能出奇地糟糕。

另一个显而易见的选择是 OpenCV，但我对在大学使用它有一些不好的回忆（也许它只是 C++ 上下文……），而且 Haskell 绑定看起来相当痛苦。

因此，我的下一个实验是使用原生 Haskell 图像处理库 Hip。 在其作者 @lehins 本人和 @HanStolpo 的帮助下，我们能够使其在 ZuriHac 发挥作用！ （再次感谢！）

然而，它仍然缺少一些我想要的功能，例如使用大津方法的二值化。 虽然在 Hip 中实现这一点当然是可能的，但我（这一次）觉得 Haskell 的抽象并不能真正帮助完成手头的任务，而且只会让事情变得不必要的复杂化。 相比之下，C 语言的 for 循环在概念上非常简单，并且与 Haskell 代码一样快。 幸运的是，C 是 Haskell 中的一等公民，并且很容易捆绑一些 C 代码并通过 Haskell 的 FFI 调用它。

不幸的是，似乎没有一个简单的 C 库可以让我连接到 Perspec 而不会引起太多 FFI 的麻烦，因此我开始研究 FlatCV——一个用于计算机视觉和图像处理的纯 C 库。

我在这里的牦牛剃毛可能有点过头了，但既然整个项目无论如何都是一种爱的劳动，为什么不一路走下去呢？ 😅

我对使用 C 语言进行图像处理算法的体验感到非常满意，并且我能够使用必要的 Haskell 绑定快速构建一个功能齐全的版本。 就在最近，我发布了 0.3.0 版本，现在它已经具备了图像处理库所期望的大部分基本操作。 我还移植了一些更高级别的 CV 操作，例如我首先在 Perspectra 中实现的自适应二值化和角点检测。

仍然有很多机会可以提高 FlatCV 的性能：SIMD、GPU 使用、流处理等。但是，由于 FlatCV 不是在实时环境（即 60 fps）中使用，因此性能已经绰绰有余。

有了 FlatCV，我终于可以实现 1.0 的最后一个缺失部分：直接在 Perspec 中自动角点检测。

边缘检测与角点检测

大多数扫描仪应用程序都会使用 Dropbox 描述的管道来检测文档：

  1. 缩小图像
  2. 运行边缘检测算法（例如 Canny）
  3. 使用霍夫变换找到最突出的直线
  4. 从这些线的交点构建四边形并对它们进行评分以选择最佳的四边形

这对于高对比度背景上完美平坦的纸张非常有效。 但真正的文件很少是完全平坦的：收据是皱巴巴的，书页是弯曲的，折叠后的纸张也永远不会完全平坦。 当您将直线拟合到弯曲边缘时，即使边缘检测本身是完美的，线的交点（即重建的角）也可能会非常偏离。

因此，Perspec 从另一面着手：它不是寻找直边，而是将照片分割为文档和背景，然后从文档的轮廓中导出角点。 这是 FlatCV 角点检测流程的详细信息：

  1. 将图像转换为灰度并将其缩小为 256×256 像素。 （检测不需要全分辨率，这使得检测速度更快。）
  2. 模糊图像以消除噪音和纸张纹理。
  3. 使用 Sobel 过滤器创建高程图。 （坚固的边缘成为山脊。）
  4. 使用分水岭分割淹没高程图：图像中心为文档盆地播种，图像边界为背景盆地播种。 结果是文档的二进制掩码。
  5. 使用二元闭合平滑蒙版。
  6. 在面罩上运行 Förstner 角点检测器。 （与更流行的 Harris 检测器不同，其角向内移动，Förstner 检测器产生亚像素精度的角位置。）
  7. 对候选角进行排序，保留角度最大的 4 个角。
  8. 将角坐标缩放回原始分辨率。
Input 检测到的角点

这种方法的好处是它从不假设边缘是直的。 分水岭很高兴地遵循褶皱的文档边界，即使在皱巴巴的收据上，角落仍然局部明确定义。

如果检测确实出错，您只需将选择多边形拖动到正确的大小和位置即可。 两全其美：自动检测和手动校正。

二值化算法

纠正观点只是故事的一半。 对于文档和收据，另一半是将照片转换为干净的黑白图像。 这就是 Perspec 中的“保存 BW”和“保存 BW 平滑”按钮的作用。

这项任务听起来很简单：每个比某个阈值暗的像素都会变成黑色，而其他所有像素都会变成白色。 棘手的部分是选择阈值。

经典的解决方案是大津方法：它构建图像中所有灰度值的直方图，然后选择最能区分暗像素（文本）和亮像素（纸张）的阈值。 这个效果很好…… 以获得均匀照明的图像。

不幸的是，照片很少是均匀照明的。 通常，手持相机的人或相机本身会产生亮度梯度或阴影。

文档扫描文献充满了局部自适应算法（例如 Niblack 和 Sauvola），它们根据每个像素的邻域计算其单独的阈值。

然而，FlatCV 的智能黑白转换使用了一种更简单的技巧来摆脱单一全局阈值：它在阈值处理之前删除阴影。

  1. 将图像转换为灰度。
  2. 创建它的严重模糊副本（模糊半径约为图像大小的 10%）。 所有文本和细节都被平均掉，剩下的基本上只是照明：亮度梯度和柔和的阴影。
  3. 从灰度图像中减去模糊副本。 这会保留高频（文本）并删除低频（阴影）。 结果是得到均匀照明的图像。
  4. 应用使用大津方法计算的全局阈值。

对于打印文档的照片，我发现它的效果与更复杂的本地自适应算法一样好，甚至更好，同时实现起来更快、更简单。

“保存黑白”按钮恰好应用此管道并将结果存储为真正的 1 位黑白图像，其中每个像素要么全黑，要么全白。

新的“保存黑白平滑”按钮更进一步，使用两个阈值（大津阈值 ± 小偏移量）：低于下阈值的像素变为黑色，高于上阈值的像素变为白色，而介于两者之间的像素保持缩放的灰度值。 这会产生抗锯齿边缘，因此文本看起来不会锯齿，而文件大小几乎保持不变。 这就是为什么它是文档、收据和白板的推荐选项。

1.0 中还有哪些新内容

自动角点检测是主要功能，但 1.0 版本中还添加了很多其他功能：

  • 支持Windows。 随着 macOS 和 Linux 的覆盖，Perspec 现在可以在所有 3 个主要桌面操作系统上运行。

  • 新的“选择文件”视图，带有按钮和拖放支持以选择图像。
  • 新的“保存黑白平滑”导出选项可将图像转换为抗锯齿黑白图像。 现在，这是文档、收据和白板的推荐选项。
  • 现在还可以处理 PNG 的 EXIF 旋转数据。
  • 升级到最新版本的 Brillo，带来了改进的应用程序设计、按钮悬停效果和每个操作系统的默认字体。

安装

发布页面上还提供了适用于 macOS、Windows 和 Linux 的预构建二进制文件，在 macOS 上，您可以通过我的 Homebrew Tap 安装它：

brew install --cask ad-si/tap/perspec

但是，您仍然需要购买许可证才能摆脱这些版本中的升级横幅。

您可以在 itch.io 或 Gumroad 上购买 Perspec 的许可证。 这将为您提供许可证密钥，从而消除应用程序中烦人的“请购买许可证”消息。

即使您自己不需要该软件，也请考虑购买它作为支持 Haskell 桌面应用程序和计算机视觉软件开发的一种方式。

安装后，您可以将图像拖放到应用程序窗口或通过 CLI 进行批处理：

perspec fix photos/*.jpeg
